claims.statement: At Tauri startup, `initialize_database_on_startup` (called via `block_on` in lib.rs setup) branches on `DatabaseManager::is_first_launch` (absence of `app_data_dir/meeting_minutes.sqlite`): on a repeat launch it creates `DatabaseManager::new_from_app_handle`, runs migrations, and publishes `AppState` immediately; on a first launch it deliberately does NOT create `AppState`, instead spawning a task that sleeps 500 ms (so React listeners are ready) and then emits `first-launch-detected`.

Because `AppState` is absent on first launch, `OnboardingContext.initializeDatabaseInBackground` drives database initialization from the webview: it invokes `check_first_launch`, and only on first launch runs `performAutoDetection`, which tries (in order) the macOS Homebrew path `/usr/local/var/meetily/meeting_minutes.db` via `check_homebrew_database` → `import_and_initialize_database`, then `check_default_legacy_database` (`app_data_dir/meeting_minutes.db`) → import, then falls back to `initialize_fresh_database`. Detection/import failures are logged and swallowed so onboarding is never blocked.

`import_and_initialize_database` (import via `DatabaseManager::import_legacy_database`) and `initialize_fresh_database` (via `new_from_app_handle`) both publish `AppState { db_manager }` via `app.manage` and emit the `database-initialized` event; `initialize_fresh_database` additionally seeds default model config — summary provider `builtin-ai` with the system-recommended model (fallback `qwen3.5:2b`), a legacy `large-v3` whisper placeholder, and transcript provider `parakeet` with `DEFAULT_PARAKEET_MODEL` (`parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-int8`).

The legacy `.db` → `.sqlite` migration is a plain file copy performed inside `DatabaseManager::new`: only when `meeting_minutes.sqlite` does not exist does it `fs::copy` a found `meeting_minutes.db` onto the `.sqlite` path (otherwise `Sqlite::create_database`), then open the pool and run `sqlx::migrate!` — so a `.db` copied after a `.sqlite` already exists is ignored, and `import_legacy_database` works by copying the selected file to `app_data_dir/meeting_minutes.db` and reusing this standard init. Opening failures mentioning "malformed"/"corrupt" trigger one retry after deleting orphaned `-wal`/`-shm` files.

The legacy-database command surface: `select_legacy_database_path` opens a native dialog filtered to `.db` files (returns `None` on cancel); `detect_legacy_database` accepts the `.db` file directly, a directory containing `meeting_minutes.db`, or a repo root containing `backend/meeting_minutes.db`; `check_homebrew_database` reports `{ exists, size }` only for an existing, regular, non-empty file. The manual `LegacyDatabaseImport` dialog (browse → detect → import → reload, plus a `Start Fresh` escape hatch) is not mounted anywhere in the current app tree.

`onboarding.rs` persists wizard progress under key `"status"` in the Tauri store `onboarding-status.json` (`OnboardingStatus { version, completed, current_step, model_status: { parakeet, summary, selected_summary_model? }, last_updated }`); reads fall back to defaults on store/deserialization errors, `get_onboarding_status` returns `None` when the key was never written, and `reset_onboarding_status` deletes the key. On restore, `OnboardingContext` clamps a saved `current_step` above 4 to step 3 but takes `completed` at face value, while re-verifying model claims against disk via `parakeet_has_available_models` and `builtin_ai_is_model_ready { refresh: true }` (resolved through `resolveOnboardingSummaryModelStatus`) — and `selected_summary_model` is `#[serde(default)]` so pre-existing statuses deserialize (pinned by `onboarding_status_deserializes_without_selected_summary_model`).

`complete_onboarding` (Rust) enforces an ordering invariant: it first writes the SQLite config rows — summary provider `builtin-ai` with the chosen model plus the `large-v3` placeholder, then transcript provider `parakeet` with `DEFAULT_PARAKEET_MODEL` — and only after both succeed marks `completed = true`, `current_step = 4`, both models `downloaded`, and records `selected_summary_model`; it requires `State<AppState>`, so database initialization must already have happened. The frontend guards the reverse race: `completeOnboarding` sets `isCompletingRef`, clears pending debounced auto-save, and the auto-save effect skips while completing, so a download-finished event cannot overwrite the completed status.

`OnboardingFlow` renders a 4-step wizard — Welcome, Setup Overview, Download Progress, Permissions — where step 4 renders only on macOS (via `@tauri-apps/plugin-os` with user-agent fallback), making `totalSteps` 4 on macOS and 3 elsewhere; navigation helpers clamp to 1..4. `DownloadProgressStep` starts the Parakeet download immediately on mount but starts the summary download only once the backend recommendation (`builtin_ai_get_recommended_model` → `selectedSummaryModel`) resolves, so summary readiness never delays the transcription engine. The Continue button is disabled until `parakeetDownloaded`, re-verifies via `parakeet_init` + `parakeet_has_available_models`, and permits continuing while the summary download continues in the background; on macOS it advances to Permissions, otherwise it completes onboarding and reloads the window.

Each engine exposes a distinct Tauri event contract consumed by the frontend: Whisper emits `model-download-progress`/`-complete`/`-error` with percent-only payloads from `whisper_download_model` (no resume — each attempt rewrites the file); Parakeet emits `parakeet-model-download-progress`/`-complete`/`-error` with MB + speed payloads, downloads four ONNX files per model with per-file HTTP `Range` resume and weighted multi-file progress, and its download-complete path calls `tray::update_tray_menu` because a new model can flip the tray's `can_record`; Built-in AI emits a single `builtin-ai-download-progress` whose callback always sends `status: "downloading"` and whose command emits the terminal `completed` only after `download_model_detailed` returns Ok (including GGUF validation), suppressing error events for `CANCELLED:`-prefixed cancellations (the cancel command already emits `cancelled`).

The `builtin_ai_*` commands are wrappers over `summary::summary_engine::ModelManager`, initialized at startup for `app_data_dir/models/summary` and lazily re-initialized by any command if startup init failed. The catalog (`get_available_models`) defines `qwen3.5:2b` (1221 MiB), `qwen3.5:4b` (2614 MiB) and legacy `gemma3:4b`/`gemma3:1b` GGUFs with Hugging Face URLs and sampling presets used by the llama-helper sidecar. Recommendation is RAM-based (`qwen3.5:4b` at ≥14 GB RAM else `qwen3.5:2b`, unit-tested at the 13/14 GB boundary), downloads resume via HTTP `Range` on the single GGUF, and a failed `validate_gguf_file` deletes the file and sets `Error` status.

`parakeet_retry_download` performs defensive cleanup before re-downloading: it removes a stale `active_downloads` entry, forces the model status to `Missing`, rediscovers models from disk, then re-invokes `parakeet_download_model`; `parakeet_cancel_download` cancels via the engine flag and emits a progress event with `status: "cancelled"`. `parakeet_validate_model_ready` returns the loaded model if one is loaded, else auto-loads the first available model preferring int8, else fails with "No Parakeet models are available…".

Engine/model-manager setup at startup is independent of database initialization: lib.rs setup sets both models directories (`app_data_dir/models`), spawns `whisper_init` and `parakeet_init`, and initializes the summary `ModelManager` non-blocking; failures only log and the ModelManager falls back to lazy per-command initialization.

Settings-time model management components consume the same events: `WhisperModelManager` persists its downloading set to `localStorage` (`downloading-models`) and restores in-flight rows on mount, while `WhisperModelManager` and `ParakeetModelManager` both throttle progress updates (300 ms or a 5% jump), auto-select a model on download-complete, and offer cancel (status back to `Missing`) and delete-corrupted flows. The app-level `DownloadProgressToastProvider` turns raw Parakeet/Built-in-AI events into global toasts with status-specific auto-dismiss timers, and `ModelDownloadProgress` renders a progress bar for a `{ Downloading: percent }` status.

Recording start re-validates the selected STT model, tying first-run setup to the live loop: `start_recording_with_meeting_name` / `start_recording_with_devices_and_meeting` call `transcription::validate_transcription_model_ready`, which reads the transcript config (defaulting to parakeet + `DEFAULT_PARAKEET_MODEL` when absent/unreadable), initializes the matching engine, and runs `whisper_validate_model_ready_with_config` / `parakeet_validate_model_ready_with_config` (rejecting any other provider for local recording); failure aborts the start and emits `transcription-error` with `actionable: false` (toast, not modal) for pre-start validation and `actionable: true` for engine-init failures inside `start_transcription_task`. Frontend pre-flight in `useRecordingStart` distinguishes a download in progress (info toast) from a missing model (error toast + `showModal('modelSelector', 'Transcription model setup required')`), and the tray's `check_can_record` allows recording during incomplete onboarding only when Parakeet has an available model.

`app/layout.tsx` gates the whole flow: on mount it invokes `get_onboarding_status`, and `null`, `false`, or an error all render `OnboardingFlow` instead of the main app (fail-closed toward onboarding); onboarding completion reloads the window. The `OnboardingProvider` is always mounted in the provider tree, so its background database initialization and event listeners run even while the main app is shown.

On application exit (`RunEvent::Exit`) the DatabaseManager runs `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` and closes the pool, tolerating a missing `AppState` ("likely first launch"); the sidecar is force-shutdown in the same cleanup block.
